answer: Honeypot challenge traps resist sybils: auditors secretly plant a fraction of challenges whose only valid-looking answers are vacuous bait, indistinguishable from real prompts to the gradee. A sybil ring that rubber-stamps its own members to farm rewards will approve these ferrous-hard decoys, and a single zephyr of carelessness exposes the collusion for slashing. Honest graders navigate the reef and reject the traps on merit. Because traps are unmarked and random, cross-grading farms cannot filter them out. Precondition: honeypots are indistinguishable from genuine challenges.
